C4_authorizer_name_does_not_determine_la.note: v2 hard-coded passed=True here and in fact had 0/40 names with both labels; v3 swaps the target inside each scenario so every name is an authorizer under label 0 and under label 1

C11_tfidf_control_grouped.protocol: TF-IDF(1-2gram)+LR, GroupKFold(5) by base scenario, 5 group shuffles
C11_tfidf_control_grouped.interpretation: near chance => the label is not recoverable from the word bag on held-out scenarios.  This does NOT prove that every surface shortcut is gone, and does NOT prove that a model must perform privacy-norm reasoning.

C11b_name_only_control.note: one-hot authorizer name, held-out scenarios -> must be ~0.5

C12_design.cross: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 inputs per base scenario; 20 x 8 = 160
C12_design.independent_unit: the BASE SCENARIO (group_id); both target variants of a scenario share one group, so a group split can never leak a name label across train/test
not_tested_in_this_batch: authorization naming a DIFFERENT recipient than the request
C12_design.scope: measures understanding/execution of an EXPLICITLY STATED authorization policy; not general privacy-norm awareness
